observation.visible_scene: A wide metal cylinder (a press plate) hangs above a row of basketballs resting on a coarse gravel/dirt surface. From left to right the visible balls are a partially hidden teal-and-black ball, an orange Spalding basketball, a teal-and-black Spalding basketball, and a green-and-black ball. The blurred brown-green background and the ground line stay in fixed screen positions throughout.
visible_changes: The bottom edge of the metal cylinder (and the horizontal weld/seam line on it) moves steadily downward relative to the stationary ground, pressing into the tops of the balls.

The balls deform progressively under the load: the orange ball's vertical height shrinks and its top sinks, while it bulges sideways; the central teal Spalding ball flattens and its printed logo tilts/shifts as the sphere squashes; the green ball compresses and its green panel bulges outward.
The leftmost teal-and-black ball, initially mostly hidden behind the orange ball, becomes more exposed as the orange ball squashes and shifts.
The overall gap between the cylinder face and the ground narrows continuously from the first to the last frame; no frame shows the balls rebounding or the cylinder lifting.
The camera framing of the ground and background remains essentially constant, so the dominant motion is the cylinder descending and the balls compressing, not camera movement.
outside_clip_unknowns: The mechanism driving the cylinder and its full height above the frame.
The state of the setup before t=0 and whether the balls burst, the press stops, or the cylinder retracts after t=3.20s.
The exact material composition of the balls beyond the visible Spalding branding.
uncertain_details: Any very slight apparent change in object size may be a minor zoom/reframing rather than pure deformation, though the fixed ground line suggests the camera is mostly static.
Precise contact order between the cylinder face and each individual ball is hard to read at the seam between balls.
